summary.tldr: Removes Senate property rules, including the $4,000 net worth test and the real property rule for senators outside Quebec.
what_it_does: Repeals the rule that senators must have real and personal property worth at least $4,000 above debts.
Ends the real property requirement for senators representing provinces other than Quebec.
Replaces the qualification declaration so senators no longer have to swear that they own qualifying property.
Changes the vacancy rule so a senator no longer loses the seat for failing the property qualification.
who_it_affects: Senators from provinces other than Quebec
summary.background: The Constitution Act, 1867 sets property qualifications for senators. This bill amends those rules and updates related Senate forms and vacancy rules.
